plain.li: Cup of tea after supper. Sat with it until it went cold.
Tea in the morning, before anyone else was up.
[winter] Held a hot cup of tea in both hands until my fingers worked again.
[rain] Tea, and rain on the roof. Not a bad evening.
[child] I had tea. I put too much sugar in it.

warm.li: Made tea for whoever was still up. We sat and talked for a while.

cheerful.li: Tea! The best part of the day.

gloomy.li: A cup of tea. The one thing that went right today.

cold.li: Tea keeps the head clear. I'll have another tomorrow.

plain.li: Another quiet week at the outpost. I miss the noise of home more than I expected.
Started a letter home tonight. Kept it short: still alive, still working, food's fine.
The outpost is so quiet at night that I can hear every animal for a mile around.
[winter] Cold at the outpost. We keep the fire going day and night and count the firewood.
[outpost:Mining] Hauled stone all day. My hands are raw, and the pile keeps growing.
[outpost:Logging] Felled six trees before noon. My shoulders will feel it tomorrow.
[outpost:Farming] The rows are coming up green. I'd like the others to see them.
[outpost:Hunting] Tracked a herd for two days. Came back with meat and the smell of it in my clothes.
[outpost:Defensive] Stood watch all night. Nothing came, which is the point.
[outpost:Trading] Haggled with a caravan most of the morning. Got a fair price in the end.
[outpost:Science] Worked through my notes until the light went.
[outpost:Town] The town is busier than home. Too many new faces to learn.
[outpost:Scavenging] Dug through ruins all day. Found a few things worth carrying back.
[outpost:Encampment] A caravan stopped for the night. It was good to hear some news.

warm.li: I keep a list of things to tell everyone when I'm home. It's getting long.

cheerful.li: The outpost is coming along nicely! I'd show it off if anyone visited.

gloomy.li: Out here the days run together. I've lost count of how long I've been away.

cold.li: The outpost pays its way. I'll stay as long as it does.
